title: Model-only no-op drops media-only document changes

evidence.quote: const modelHash = sha256(modelJson); ... if (head && head.modelHash === modelHash) { return { commit: head, created: false }; } ... const fileHash = sha256(fileBytes);
A shape on a slide reduced to its text
Word/Excel/PowerPoint files are zip archives containing many parts ... every image ... media-heavy ones bloat.

reasoning: The store decides that a save is a no-op before hashing or comparing file bytes. The normalized models intentionally omit user-visible binary content such as embedded images, so a user can change a picture in a document/deck while the parsed model stays identical. That second save is silently discarded, leaving restore/export/branch switching unable to recover that file state.
reproduction: Commit an OOXML file with some text and an embedded image, then commit the same extracted text with only the image bytes changed. parseDocument/parsePptx produces the same DocModel, so SnapshotStore.commit returns created:false and the old file bytes remain the branch head.
recommendation: Do not use modelHash alone as the persistence no-op boundary. Either include hashes for user-visible non-text parts in DocModel, or compare/store fileHash as well and only treat a save as unchanged when both the semantic model and relevant file content are unchanged.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: store.test.ts only checks the no-op path with generated documents whose parsed model and bytes are effectively the same scenario; it does not create two different files that parse to the same model.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a core test that commits two OOXML byte arrays with the same parsed text model but different media/part bytes, then asserts the second commit is created and getFileBytes returns the newer bytes.
minimumFixScope: SnapshotStore.commit no-op/coalesce criteria plus model/adapters or a normalized file-content hash for visible non-text OOXML parts.
